exposure: isolated abnormal 1-hour glucose challenge test (GCT) without gestational diabetes (GDM)
intermediate GDM screening (1-hour GCT value >= 140 and < 200 mg/dL with normal 3-hour glucose tolerance test)
diagnosed GDM (1-hour GCT >= 200 mg/dL or abnormal 3-hour GTT)
outcome: composite perinatal morbidity (large for gestational age birthweight, birth injury, hypoglycemia with NICU admission, respiratory distress syndrome, transient tachypnea of the newborn, apnea, NICU admission, perinatal death)
cohort: The study included 37,277 patients who underwent GDM screening at or after 24 weeks' gestation, delivered a singleton fetus, and gave birth at an urban tertiary hospital between January 2013 and October 2021.
finding: Patients with an isolated abnormal 1-hour GCT without a GDM diagnosis were at increased risk for adverse pregnancy outcomes, similar to, though less pronounced than, those with diagnosed GDM.
mod_finding: Intermediate GDM screening was associated with an increased risk for cesarean delivery (aOR 1.18, 95% CI 1.10-1.26), which was further pronounced in those with GDM.
